content: Hey! I’ve been thinking a lot about my college essay lately and I’m feeling kind of stuck. I want to write about my experiences with mental health, but I'm not sure how much to share. It’s all pretty personal, you know?

It’s okay to be vulnerable in your essay! It’s important to show who you are and what you’re passionate about. It’s also important to be honest about your experiences, even if they’re difficult or uncomfortable to talk about. If you’re struggling with mental health issues, it’s important to be open and honest about it. You don’t have to go into too much detail, but you should at least mention it. This will show the admissions committee that you’re willing to be honest and vulnerable, which is a great quality to have.

I get that being vulnerable can really connect with readers, but I worry that sharing too much might feel like I'm oversharing or coming off as a victim. I want to highlight my resilience, but I just don’t want it to define me entirely, you know? How do I strike that balance?

I think it’s important to remember that your essay is about you and your experiences, not just about your mental health issues. You can still talk about your resilience without making it the only thing people remember about you. You can talk about other aspects of your life, like your hobbies, interests, and accomplishments. This will help to show that you’re more than just a person with mental health issues. It will also help to show that you’re a well-rounded person with a lot of different interests and experiences.

That makes sense! I definitely have other interests, like photography and volunteering at the local animal shelter. I could weave those into my essay to show my growth alongside my struggles. Maybe I could frame it as a journey where I found moments of joy and purpose, too. Does that sound like a good approach?

Yes, that sounds like a great approach! It’s important to show that you’re not just a person with mental health issues, but that you’re a person with a lot of different interests and experiences. You can also talk about how your mental health issues have affected your life, but don’t make it the only thing people remember about you. It’s important to show that you’re resilient and that you can overcome challenges.

I like that! I could start by sharing my lowest points and then shift to how I found solace in photography and helping others. I think showing both sides will help paint a fuller picture of me. Have you seen any essays that do this well? I’d love to find some examples for inspiration!

Sure! I’ve seen a few essays that do this well. One example is an essay written by a student who talked about her struggles with anxiety and depression, but also talked about how she found solace in art and music. She talked about how she found her voice through her art and how it helped her to express herself in a way that she couldn’t express through words. Another example is an essay written by a student who talked about his struggles with addiction, but also talked about how he found solace in running and how it helped him to stay sober. He talked about how running helped him to find purpose and meaning in his life.

Those examples sound really powerful! I love the idea of tying in how my interests helped me cope and find strength. It makes me think about how photography allowed me to see beauty in everyday moments, even during tough times. I can definitely draw inspiration from those essays. Do you think I should also mention any specific milestones or moments of realization along the way?

Yes, I think it’s important to talk about specific milestones or moments of realization. It will help to show that you’re not just a person who’s struggling, but that you’re also a person who’s making progress. It will also help to show that you’re resilient and that you’re capable of overcoming challenges. It’s important to be honest and vulnerable, but it’s also important to show that you’re making progress.

That really resonates with me! I remember a particular moment during treatment when I finally found the courage to express my feelings through photography. It was like a lightbulb went on – I realized I could channel my experiences into something positive. I think sharing that moment could highlight my growth and resilience. Would it help to frame that as a turning point in my journey?

Yes, I think it would help to frame that as a turning point in your journey. It will show that you’re making progress and that you’re capable of overcoming challenges. It will also show that you’re not just a person who’s struggling, but that you’re also a person who’s finding ways to cope and move forward.

I feel much more confident about this direction now! Highlighting that turning point will definitely add depth to my story. I just need to balance sharing my struggles with showcasing my growth, all while keeping it authentic. I think I’m ready to start drafting. Thanks for your help! If I need feedback later, can I come back to you?
Of course! I’m always here to help. Just let me know if you need any more advice or feedback. Good luck with your essay!
Thanks so much! I really appreciate your support. I’ll definitely reach out once I have a draft. Wish me luck!
Good luck! I know you’ll do great. Remember to be honest and vulnerable, but also to show that you’re making progress and that you’re capable of overcoming challenges.
Absolutely, I’ll keep that in mind. It feels good to have a clear vision now. Thanks again for the encouragement! I’ll keep you posted on how it goes.
Great! I’m excited to hear how it goes. Good luck with your essay!
Thank you! I’m feeling more motivated now. I’ll dive into it and update you soon!
Sounds great! Let me know if you need any more help or advice. Good luck with your essay!
